title: Measure-only preserving Markov transports characterize mass-stationarity
author: Alec Kriebel
abstract: Let G be a locally compact second countable Hausdorff Abelian group, acting jointly measurably on an arbitrary measurable space. Let Q be sigma-finite and let ξ be a covariant locally finite Radon random measure, nonzero Q-almost everywhere. We prove that full ambient Q-invariance under every invariant, ξ-preserving, ξ-measurable Markov transport kernel implies the joint Mecke identity, and hence mass-stationarity. Together with known transport invariance this answers Last–Thorisson's Problem 7.3 in the stated setting. The argument uses oriented local symmetric transports away from periods of the measure and normalized period-subgroup transports on the remaining set. It requires neither a standard Borel ambient space nor a sigma-finite law of ξ, and imposes no finite-intensity assumption.
short_summary: Measure-only randomized transports that preserve mass characterize when the origin is typical in that mass, while retaining the full ambient state.
plain_language_draft: A mass-stationary origin is a location that is typical of the mass around it. This note studies randomized changes of origin that redistribute the mass without changing it. The claimed result says that if every such rule leaves the full environment unchanged in law, even when the rule can inspect only the mass measure, then the origin is mass-stationary. The proof treats translations that preserve the mass measure separately, because those translations can still change other information in the environment.
exact_result_draft: For a locally compact second countable Hausdorff Abelian group acting jointly measurably on an arbitrary measurable space, a sigma-finite measure Q and a covariant locally finite Radon random measure ξ that is nonzero Q-almost everywhere, full ambient invariance under every invariant ξ-preserving ξ-measurable Markov transport is equivalent to joint mass-stationarity. The sufficient direction derives the joint Mecke identity.
interesting_result: The kernels observe only ξ, yet their invariance tests constrain the entire ambient state, including states changed by translations that leave ξ fixed. Standard Borel structure is needed for the canonical Radon-measure space, not for the arbitrary ambient space.
attribution_draft: The proof addresses Last and Thorisson’s formal Problem7.3 (Annals of Probability,2009). Mecke/Palm equivalence, Palm/mass-stationarity equivalence and the converse invariance statement are credited classical inputs. The claimed new step derives joint Mecke reversal from the measure-only Markov hypothesis. Earlier discrete/aperiodic and positive-density cases receive explicit credit.
limits_draft: The theorem requires local finiteness, nonzero mass, sigma-finite Q and an Abelian group. It includes atoms, diffuse or mixed mass, periodic measures, infinite total mass and infinite Q. It does not assume finite intensity or a sigma-finite marginal law of ξ. It does not resolve the narrower deterministic Cox-allocation converse or establish current openness or worldwide priority.
follow_up_reason: No independently substantiated paper-worthy conjecture meeting the high bar was identified in this scope review. The narrower Cox-allocation problem is expressly outside the result and its current unresolved status has not been established here.
